before: **Flat-tax income.** Interest, dividends and gains on shares, bonds, funds and derivatives ([§ 20(1) and (2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__20.html)). Gain = sale proceeds, less costs directly tied to the sale, less purchase cost. Foreign-currency amounts are converted at the date of each transaction. For securities of one kind in one custody account, the first bought count as the first sold (§ 20(4) EStG).
after:
**Flat-tax income.** Interest, dividends and gains on shares, bonds, funds and derivatives ([§ 20(1) and (2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__20.html)). Gain = sale proceeds, less costs directly tied to the sale, less purchase cost. Foreign-currency amounts are converted at the date of each transaction. For securities of one kind in one custody account, the first bought count as the first sold (§ 20(4) EStG).

**Mandatory financing exceptions (§ 32d(2) no. 1).** Before applying 25%, test income within § 20(1) nos. 4 and 7 and § 20(2) sentence 1 nos. 4 and 7. Under (a), creditor and debtor must be related within the statutory test, and the corresponding debtor expenses must be business expenses or income-related costs connected with income subject to German tax, without the § 20(9) sentence 1 second-half expense bar applying. Under (b), the same debtor-expense/German-tax conditions apply to payments by a corporation or cooperative to a shareholder holding at least 10%, or to a person related to that shareholder. Exactly 10% meets the ownership limb; 9.99% does not meet that limb alone, and (a)/(c) still require testing. Do not establish statutory relatedness from family membership alone.

Under (c), test third-party capital income connected with capital made available to the creditor's business; the stated extension covers a related person, a partnership in which the creditor/related person is a co-entrepreneur, or a corporation/cooperative in which either holds at least 10%, subject to the third party's recourse condition. A common plan, particularly close timing or linked interest agreements, is relevant; the statutory connection is absent where interest terms are market-standard or the flat-tax treatment gives no tax-burden advantage. The clauses apply correspondingly where the capital finances income under § 2(1) sentence 1 nos. 4, 6 or 7. Establish those actual financing/recourse/terms facts rather than treating every owner or family loan alike.

For an actually qualifying no. 1 case, the ordinary tariff applies and § 20(6)/(9) does not apply: use eligible actual costs rather than the Sparer-Pauschbetrag method. Stipulated qualifying interest of EUR 10,000 less EUR 2,000 eligible actual costs gives EUR 8,000 ordinary-rate income, rather than EUR 9,000 from an assumed EUR 1,000 allowance; final tax depends on the other tariff inputs. This mandatory route is distinct from the optional dividend partial-income election.

before: 7. On a sale, lump sums already taxed are deducted from the gain ([§ 19(1) InvStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/invstg_2018/__19.html)). With a foreign broker the client tracks them.
after: 7. On a sale, deduct the full Vorabpauschalen assessed during ownership from the gain before applying the actual partial exemption ([§ 19(1) InvStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/invstg_2018/__19.html)). Use the full assessed amount regardless of partial exemption or whether allowances prevented cash withholding, not merely its taxable fraction; do not deduct unassessed estimates. A stipulated gain of EUR 10,000 less EUR 1,120 full prior assessed Vorabpauschalen leaves EUR 8,880; a 30% equity-fund exemption then leaves EUR 6,216. Deducting only EUR 784 would wrongly leave EUR 6,451.20. Obtain actual broker history, including with a foreign broker.

before: **Large holdings (§ 17 EStG).** A sale of shares in any company, German or foreign, is business income if the seller held at least 1%, directly or indirectly, at any time in the five years before the sale ([§ 17(1)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__17.html): "zu mindestens 1 Prozent beteiligt war"). A holding cut below 1% still counts, and gifted shares count if the giver met the test. Liquidation and capital repayments count as a sale (§ 17(4)). Under the partial-income method (Teileinkünfteverfahren), 60% of the price less 60% of cost and selling costs is taxable ([§ 3 no. 40 c](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3.html), [§ 3c(2)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3c.html)), less the allowance: the share sold of EUR 9,060, cut by the gain above the same share of EUR 36,100. The result joins other income at the normal rate. A loss is 60% deductible and can offset other income, but is barred in part for shares received free or not in a qualifying holding for the full five years (§ 17(2)).
after: **Large holdings (§ 17 EStG).** A sale of shares in any company, German or foreign, is business income if the seller held at least 1%, directly or indirectly, at any time in the five years before the sale ([§ 17(1)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__17.html): "zu mindestens 1 Prozent beteiligt war"). A holding cut below 1% still counts. If the seller acquired the disposed share free within the five years before disposal, § 17(1) sentence 4 applies sentence 1 correspondingly where the seller did not personally meet the test but a predecessor, or an earlier predecessor in a chain of free transfers, held the statutory participation within the relevant five-year period. Record the actual acquisition and predecessor holding dates; a free acquisition outside that recent-acquisition window does not enter this exception solely because its giver currently owns 1%. This share test is separate from AStG residence aggregation. Liquidation and capital repayments count as a sale (§ 17(4)). Under the partial-income method (Teileinkünfteverfahren), 60% of the price less 60% of cost and selling costs is taxable ([§ 3 no. 40 c](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3.html), [§ 3c(2)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__3c.html)), less the allowance: the share sold of EUR 9,060, cut by the gain above the same share of EUR 36,100. The result joins other income at the normal rate. A loss is 60% deductible and can offset other income, but is barred in part for shares received free or not in a qualifying holding for the full five years (§ 17(2)).

before: - Land and buildings sold "nicht mehr als zehn Jahre" after purchase; other assets (crypto, gold, foreign currency, collectibles) sold "nicht mehr als ein Jahr" after purchase ([§ 23(1)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__23.html)). Exactly one year is still taxable.
after: - Land and buildings sold "nicht mehr als zehn Jahre" after purchase; other assets (crypto, gold, foreign currency, collectibles) sold "nicht mehr als ein Jahr" after purchase ([§ 23(1)](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__23.html)). Exactly one year is still taxable. For other private assets used as an income source with income in at least one calendar year, § 23(1) no. 2 sentence 4 extends the period to ten years. The BMF's 6 March 2025 letter, paragraph 63, specifically does not apply that extension to Currency or Payment Tokens; do not extend that administrative exception to every other private asset or token classification. An independently qualifying income-producing non-token asset sold after two years is not exempt merely because one year passed.

before: - **Bank withholding settles the tax** where all income was taxed by German banks correctly. The bank pays withheld tax to its tax office by the tenth of the following month ([§ 44(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__44.html)).
after: - **Bank withholding settles the tax** where the final-withholding conditions hold and no § 32d(2) or business-income exception under § 43(5) applies; correct bank withholding alone does not make a mandatory exception final. The bank pays withheld tax to its tax office by the tenth of the following month ([§ 44(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__44.html)).

before: - **A return is required** for investment income with no German withholding, such as a foreign broker account ([§ 32d(3) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__32d.html)), and for any § 17 or § 23 gain. A return is worth filing to use an unused allowance, offset losses across banks, credit foreign tax, settle church tax or apply the Günstigerprüfung (§ 32d(4) and (6)).
after: - **A return is required** for investment income with no German withholding, such as a foreign broker account ([§ 32d(3) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__32d.html)), for the mandatory § 32d(2) no. 1 assessment route above even where tax was withheld, and for any § 17 or § 23 gain. A return is worth filing to use an unused allowance, offset losses across banks, credit foreign tax, settle church tax or apply the Günstigerprüfung (§ 32d(4) and (6)).

before: - Do you hold, or did you hold in the last five years, 1% or more of any company? Do you work for it?
after: - Do you hold, or did you hold in the last five years, 1% or more of any company? Any free acquisition within the five years before disposal, including a chain: actual acquisition dates and each predecessor's participation/holding dates? Do you work for the company?

before: - For each fund: its type and the price on 1 January. For crypto, gold and property: purchase and sale dates, and whether you lived in the property.
after: - For each fund: its type, price on 1 January and full assessed Vorabpauschalen during ownership, including amounts with no cash withholding. For crypto, gold and property: actual asset/token classification, purchase/sale dates, any income-producing use in a calendar year, and whether you lived in the property.

before: - Do you have losses carried forward or bank loss certificates, and are you planning to leave Germany?
after:
- Do you have losses carried forward or bank loss certificates, and are you planning to leave Germany?
- For financing income: actual borrower/shareholder/related-person relationships and percentages, domestic-tax/expense use, linked deposits/loans and common plan, recourse and market interest terms, plus eligible actual costs.
